_note: SpeedKills' profile (src/game/game.ts, docs/PHASE_18_PLAN_SPEEDKILLS.md): what is in play and the design that differs from the legacy game, as the owner decided it on 2026-09-26. Selection and design only: the numbers that describe a thing stay in that thing's config. A gun here is a legacy gun (`from` in the plan) with its own name, family, role and fixed optic. Every id named here must exist (tools/checks/games.ts).
name: SpeedKills
_roster: Ten guns, two a family where there are two: a hard-hitter and a fast one. Most carry the owner's friends' names. USSO is the fastest gun in the game and the hardest to control; ANAKIN the steady SMG; BOOG the sniper, whose headshot always kills. On 2026-09-30 the owner took out the fast marksman ("remove the pulsar, no need for a fast marksman, just call it marksman now") and put a pistol in its place, like Hyper Scape's Riot One: the legacy Wingman (a heavy semi-automatic with no drop-off) tuned to it, wearing the pack's second pistol (paidweapons.json). Its name, HAMMER, stands until the owner names it.

shotgun.label: Shotguns
shotgun.use: point blank, one or two shots

pistol.label: Pistol
pistol.use: six hard single shots, steady at any range

_weapons: Each gun's SpeedKills name, its role in its pair (hard or fast), and the one optic it always wears: attachments are off, fusion is the upgrade.
_ammo: Infinite reserve: every gun reloads forever and NOVA cools instead. Loot is guns and hacks only.
_fusion: The owner's numbers: a gun on the floor is level 0, and each of five fusions adds 2% damage and 10% magazine, to +10% and +50% at level 5; reload time and recoil come down 4% a level. A copy of a higher level than yours raises yours to its level. A duplicate hack lowers that hack's cooldown by cooldownStep a level, to abilityLevels. swap is a gun's draw and put-away time over the legacy data's (Phase 20, the owner 2026-09-26: switching should be quicker as a base, 1.5 to 2 times, and quicker again as a gun is levelled, like its damage and magazine): 0.667 as found, 1.5 times as quick, to 0.5 at level 5, twice as quick; then, with a swap that phases the gun out and the next in where it is held (fparms.json swap cup), 1.35 times those (the owner, 2026-09-30: "i think our swaps are too quick for how we wanted it ... it should allow for more time to be materializing"): 0.9 as found, to 0.675 at level 5, the USSO to the USSO 0.58 s and the USSO to BOOG 1.17. STRYDER's 0.6 s draw is 0.54 s as found and 0.41 s at level 5. Ours.
_abilities: Ten hacks in two slots: pick one mobility and one utility before the match; in the battle royale, hacks on the floor fuse (the same one) or swap (another of the slot). `from` is the legacy ability each is built on; null is new. No passives, no ultimates.

set.blurb: Up, then down onto a spot, hurting whoever is under it.

_life: No knockdowns; the first death goes to the Gulag, a later one makes a ghost, revived by a squad mate at its echo marker in reviveSeconds, awaySlowdown times as long while the ghost is further than followRadius metres from the reviver; two ghost revives a match. A squad is out when none of it is alive or in the Gulag. In solo a second death is the end. A ghost moves at ghostSpeed times a player's pace and sees enemies within ghostSight metres; a restored player stands up on their echo with restoreHealth and their shield coming back.
_health: 100 health and 50 shield. The shield starts back shieldDelay seconds after the last damage and fills in shieldFill; health comes back at healthRegen a second after healthDelay. No heal items, no armour loot.
_match: The battle royale: up to maxPlayers in squads of team by default, about 6 to 7 minutes long (the owner's numbers). teams are the lobby's sizes as br.json's teams are, the bot counts each a whole number of squads with the default filling the match to 30 with your squad; bleed 0 is no knockdowns (a death is a death: the Gulag and the ghost are the second chances).
_bots: Five tiers, easiest first, by the code's ids; botNames is what SpeedKills calls each (Casual, Skilled and Advanced are the legacy Easy, Normal and Hard; Beginner and Extreme are the ends).
_brDefaults: The battle royale row as everyone starts it (the owner, 2026-09-29): duos, battle royale rules, friends as one squad (the row's first choice, never stored), 28 bots, the ring at its normal pace, landing with your loadout, and Casual bots. The owner asked for 27 bots; duos come in whole pairs, so the row offers 20, 28 and 34, and 28 is the nearest (29 in the match, 30 with a friend). A browser that has not seen `tag` has these written over what it had, once (main.ts applyBrDefaults), so a choice made after that is kept.
_botTierSpeed: A tier's speed times this, on top of botSpeedScale (bots.ts speed): Casual (easy) at 0.75, so a bot is easier to follow with the eye and the gun while players learn the game (the owner, 2026-09-29: "make the bots move like 0.75x speed so they are easier to track for everyone to start"). A tier not named moves as it did.
_lists: The lists the legacy game keeps in its own configs, in SpeedKills' guns: what the bots carry (every gun, in turn), the six default loadouts' two guns (the order of the legacy defaults: Assault, Close Quarters, Marksman, Heavy, Sidearms, Dirt Bike), and the Gulag's pool, from which the two fighters' shared pair is drawn. loadoutNames are the six defaults' names in SpeedKills (Phase 20 A7): the legacy Sidearms and Dirt Bike no longer fit guns that are STRYDER with HAMMER and BOOG with ANAKIN (the Marksman default was PULSAR with PANDA until the owner took PULSAR out on 2026-09-30: HAEFY with PANDA now, and HAEFY's place beside USSO went to HAMMER beside STRYDER, so every gun is in a default). botRename renames the bots whose names are a gun's (BOT NOVA beside the gun NOVA). The first default is USSO and BOOG (the owner, 2026-09-29): the two guns finished to the bar every gun will be held to, in first person and on the soldier, so they are what a new player and a friend opening an invite pick up first; loadoutPick moves a returning player onto it once (src/game/loadouts.ts).
_tuning: Each gun's SpeedKills tuning over its legacy numbers, as multipliers: damage (every range), fireRate, and recoil (the kick's pitch and yaw, base and random), and mag (the magazine, before fusion: USSO's 18 became 27, since at its damage a kill took 25 rounds and a reload, 3.1 s, and a fused magazine then took the reload away, a jump the TTK check rightly refused). headshotDamage, where given, is a headshot's damage outright. Set from a measured table (tools/checks/ttk.ts): at 80% of rounds on target against 150 (100 health, 50 shield), the rifles, SMGs and NOVA kill in 1.3 to 1.8 s at close range (the owner's longer, Hyper Scape-like fights; the legacy numbers were about 0.9 s), the shotguns in 0.8 to 1.4 and the marksman guns in 1.2 to 2.4. Each pair keeps its identity: PANDA slower and steadier than STRYDER; USSO the fastest gun and the hardest to hold (recoil 1.6), ANAKIN the easiest (0.6). BOOG's headshot is 450: a kill through full health, full shield and an ARMOR hack's 60% cut, at any level, as the owner asked. HAMMER is Hyper Scape's Riot One as the guides give it (26 a shot against Hyper Scape's 120 health, half as much again to the head, six rounds, no drop-off, almost no recoil; a kill in one magazine unlevelled): the same five body hits a kill against our 150 is 32.5 a shot, the Wingman's 50 at 0.65, its five rounds at 1.2 and its kick at a quarter, its own 1.5 headshot and flat damage kept, and its own 2.8 shots a second, since the guides say only that it is slow to fire. At 80% on target that is six rounds, one magazine, 1.8 s. 26 as it stood took eight and a reload (4.6 s), and fused to a nine-round magazine lost the reload (2.1 s), the jump the TTK check refuses.
_loot: The battle royale's floor (src/game/loot.ts): guns and hack cores, nothing else (the owner: loot is never homework). spots is how many places to find something each sector has: the centre, THE SPIRE, is the hot drop, the most and the best of it; the rest are the same. A spot holds a gun with gunChance and a hack core with hackChance (at least one of the two). A gun is found at fusion level 0, or higher by the tier's odds, one number a level (0, 1, 2, 3); a hack core the same way by hackOdds. A gun's colour on the floor is its level: 0 white, 1 blue, 2 purple, 3 gold. maxFloor is the highest floor a spot is put on, metres: the city's roofs run to 32 m in the mid-rise and 60 m on the downtown's lower towers, and the high ground is where the fights are (Hyper Scape: "any floor lower than a rooftop might as well be lava"), so the loot goes up there too. restock is the centre's loot coming back, as Hyper Scape's Red Tiger's did in its third season ("weapons and hacks quickly respawn at the Red Tiger landmark"): every `every` seconds of the fight the host counts the guns and hack cores left in the hot zone, and when fewer than `below` of what it started with remain, puts a hot spot's roll back on up to `batch` of its spots with nothing within `near` metres. The centre stays worth fighting for all match, and the fights come to it.

loot._carePackage: What a care package holds (brmatch.ts podItems, loot.ts speedkillsPackage), called as br.json's pod says: `guns` different guns off the roster and `hacks` different hack cores, each at a level drawn from its odds, one number a level (gunOdds levels 0 to 5, hackOdds 0 to 4). Each starts where the Spire's floor stops: a gun at level 3 (gold, 5% of the Spire's guns) up to 5, which otherwise only fusing reaches; a hack core at 2 (10% of the Spire's) up to 4, its top. Three things, as the legacy package holds three, and nothing of the legacy game's: its gun, gold helmet, batteries and phoenix are nothing a SpeedKills player can use.

_ship: The dropship (dropship.ts), over squad.json's: doorsIn is the seconds of flight it appears short of the city's edge, which is when its doors open. The owner: the ship starts off the map and flies at least 5 s before anyone can jump, so the loading screen and the city finish behind it; at 26 m/s, 6 s is about 156 m out. height: the ship flies at 175 m (squad.json's 140 before): the skyline's towers reach 160 m, and on about a third of the ship's lines the hull passed through a tower top (Phase 20 A5). centre: the line passes the Spire's crown deck at between near and far metres from its middle, on any side and flown either way, square to that offset so it comes no nearer (the owner, 2026-09-27: "the drop ship should always go over the middle district, can start from wherever and be slightly to any side, but we should be always able to land at the top middle building"). near: the mast on the crown reaches 180.5 m, over the ship's 175, and the ship is 27.4 m across its wings (measured off its model by tools/checks/sk-drop.ts), so 13.7 m either side of its line plus the mast's 1.1 m cap and 2 m to spare is 16.8; far: from 172 m (the ship less its 3 m exit) a level glide (14 m across and 12 down a second) reaches 37 m from the jump before it is down at the crown's 140.2 m, and the check jumps at the line's nearest point and glides onto the crown, 9 by 9 m, on every one of 60 lines. At random angles through the same points, 15 of 60 lines came nearer the mast than 17 m.
_identity: SpeedKills' face: its title and accents. skies are the hours SpeedKills offers in its Time of day setting, sky the one it starts at: the owner's neon night, and Hyper Scape's golden hour as the one other (the night stays the default, the owner's call).
_feel: How a fight feels (Phase 19 step 10). outline: the enemy under your crosshair within range metres is outlined in color, px screen pixels thick at the camera's own field of view (so a scope's zoom thins it in metres), never under min metres, and drawn back metres behind the figure along the line of sight so only its rim shows (src/game/outline.ts; Hyper Scape's red outline, the thing that makes a figure one shape against a lit facade). It was 0.02 m plus 1.2 mm a metre: through BOOG's scope at 40 m that was 13 pixels a side, the soldier's body hull came through his armour, and at 90 m he was a red shape (the owner, 2026-09-27: "this weird ball of red around them, causing us to not be able to see/track them"). back: the armour stands a few centimetres off the body. streaks: lines at the screen's edge once you are going faster than from times the sprint's speed, full at full times it, at most opacity: the speed the movement gives you, shown (Hyper Scape's air and dash read as fast; ours read as a camera sliding). Ours, by eye. (Phase 20 A15: with the sprint doubled and a slide 1.15 times it, the streaks start at 1.05 times the sprint and are full at 1.6.)
_viewmodel: The first-person gun (src/game/viewmodel.ts). reloadAds is how much of a reload's own roll and slide is gone while aiming, as viewmodel.json strafe.ads does for a strafe: 0.85 leaves 15%. At full size a reload in the sights rolled the gun 22 degrees at its peak and 5 to 7 at its ends, where the support hand is still on the handguard, and the 2x window swung onto it: 152 to 621 pixels of arm in the sight picture at 1280x720 on PANDA, STRYDER and NOVA (measured by the Phase 20 A3 diagnosis; 0.6 still left 172, 0.85 none). Ours, not a published number. upperArm is how much of the soldier's upper arm the first-person arms draw, from the elbow (viewmodel.json realArms upper, 0.6, for the legacy game's bodies): all of it. With the support hand under a long gun's handguard (paidweapons.json support), forearm and 0.6 of the upper arm could not reach the frame's edge, and the stub's cut end stood at the bottom of the owner's view; its points near the shoulder are weighted to the arm alone (mannequin.ts armOnly), which the first-person rig never poses, so they no longer stretch. support: the support hand on the bought guns (not a pistol's or a pump's), under the gun rather than round its side: `roll` radians about the barrel (the legacy 0.55 held it on the side, palm in), `below` metres further down than paidgun.ts puts it (22 mm over the underside, which sat the procedural glove's 4 cm grip inside the wider bought bodies), and the forearm sent toward `corner` (the gun camera's x right, y up, z back; `cornerAds` aimed) until its cut end leaves the frame, down and back under the gun rather than to the frame's lower corner (-1, -0.9, 0.6), which held the arm out to the left (the owner, 2026-09-27: "the left hand is always fucked up and the left arms sticks out too much, it should always just be supporting under the gun"). Tuned on tools/pov-sheet.ts pictures of all ten guns at 1920 by 1080 and 110 degrees. straighten: the support hand then rolls round what it holds (about the bar its knuckles lie along, pivoted on the grip, so it stays on the gun) by that share of the way to a straight wrist on the forearm, never more than `maxRoll` radians: the glove's turn and the forearm's line were each chosen alone, and the wrist took what was between them. Measured (the e2e soldier section, fparms.ts wristBend) across the ten guns: without it 44 to 83 degrees at the hip, up to 103 aimed and 122 on the USSO's rack (the owner, 2026-09-27: "look at how fucked up the left wrist is"); with it 10 to 40 at the hip, 13 to 47 aimed and 53 on the rack, the hand rolled 52 to 90 degrees round the handguard. maxRoll 1.55: at 116 degrees the Mastiff's fingers came up over the top of its pump in the sight picture. The soldier and the guns are two authors' packs (AC Game Assets' SciFiModularSoldier, Tirgames' SciFi Battle Weapons) and neither ships a hold or an animation to take the grip from. sprintPose: how much of the gun's sprint pose (lowered 13 cm, rolled 24 degrees and swung 32 across) it takes: 0.3. SpeedKills sprints whenever you move, strafing included, and at all of it the owner saw every gun "crossed and inverted" whenever he moved (2026-09-27).
_kinds: kind is each gun's two-word class, shown beside its name wherever there is room (USSO (Fast SMG)), so a beginner knows what a gun is (the owner, Phase 20 A7). Each pair reads Heavy or Steady against Fast or Auto, from its numbers (resolved at fusion 0; tools/checks/ttk.ts): PANDA 61% more a round than STRYDER and 37% slower; ANAKIN's recoil multiplier the lowest, 0.6; USSO the fastest gun at 18 a second; REZ full auto; HAEFY, the one marksman gun, is plain Marksman (the owner, 2026-09-30); HAMMER a Heavy Pistol, the one pistol; NOVA cools instead of reloading. otherKinds classes the guns the Run lends that are not in the roster.
_familiesUse: use is a family's one line on the loot card's Full view (Phase 20 A8): what the gun is for, for a player who does not know yet.
_botSpeedScale: SpeedKills' bots move at their tier's speed (bots.json) times botSpeedScale: 2, since the player's run and sprint doubled (Phase 20 A15); at their old speeds a bot could not keep up with a player, nor get away.
_botAimLagScale: A bot's aim follows its target late by its tier's aimLag (bots.json), so it trails a target running steadily by the target's speed times aimLag. A15 doubled the player's speeds, which doubled every tier's trail and about halved its hits on a runner (a body is half a metre across: Skilled trailed a legacy sprint by 1.3 m and a SpeedKills one by 2.8). SpeedKills' bots aim with aimLag times botAimLagScale, 0.5, so each tier trails a SpeedKills sprint by about what it trailed a legacy one (tools/checks/bot-aim.ts) and keeps the difficulty it was tuned to. Ours; 1 would leave every tier weaker against the new speeds.
